attempts.summary: Segmented node2 and node3 onto separate VLANs (10 and 20) over the shared link (node1 eth1 / node2 enp8s0 / node3 enp8s0), with node1 (VyOS) routing between them via 802.1Q sub-interfaces eth1.10 (10.10.10.254/24) and eth1.20 (10.10.20.254/24). node2 got enp8s0.10 (10.10.10.11/24) via NetworkManager VLAN connection 'vlan10', node3 got enp8s0.20 (10.10.20.12/24) via 'vlan20'. Static routes to the peer VLAN subnet were added on node2/node3 (via node1's VLAN gateway) with never-default so the low-metric management-network default route doesn't hijack inter-VLAN traffic. Verified cross-VLAN ping success and confirmed via tcpdump on node1's eth1 that traffic is genuinely 802.1Q-tagged (vlan 10 / vlan 20) end to end. All configs are persistent (VyOS 'save', NetworkManager connections with autoconnect). Completed the mandatory restart protocol: rebooted node1, node2, and node3 sequentially (one at a time), each confirmed via a changed /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id, with VLAN interfaces, routes, and cross-VLAN ping verified healthy after each restart.
